events.title: Agatha's Almanac - Movie Showing
events.time: 7:00 PM · Mennonite Heritage Village, 231 PTH 12N, Steinbach, MB
events.description: MHV Auxiliary presents Agatha’s Almanac Doors open 6:30 pm, coffee and refreshments served Join the MHV Auxiliary for the showing of Agatha’s Almanac, the incredible true story of 90-year-old Agatha Bock. Proceeds from the event go to the MHV Auxiliary, which supports the mission of Mennonite Heritage Village. Synopsis from Agatha’s Almanac 90-year-old Agatha forges a solitary existence on her ancestral farm, preseving heirloom seeds in her handmade universe. Without a drivers license, cell phone, running water, or even a functioning landline Agatha’s daily rituals form a vivid counterpoint to modern life. Shot by an all-female crew, the project captures the handmade materiality inherent in both the medium of film and Agatha’s tactile world. It serves as a powerful conduit for often-overlooked stories, amplifying voices and rural perspectives. Agatha’s life offers a window into the experiences of a nearly lost generation, whose value and ways of living are at risk of fading as the world rapidly changes. Tickets can be purchased online, by phone, or at the front desk.

events.title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
events.time: 7:30 PM · Kenmor Theatre, 130 7TH STREET, Morden, MB
events.description: In Tennessee Williams’ Pulitzer Prize-winning Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, the dysfunctional but wealthy Pollitt family gathers to celebrate aging patriarch Big Daddy’s birthday. But there is more to this gathering than a family reunion– Big Daddy is dying of cancer, and he hasn’t decided which of his sons will inherit the estate. His options include favorite son Brick, who drinks himself into oblivion in order to bear the oppressive expectations of his determined wife, Maggie, or his less-favored son Gooper, his fertile wife Mae, and their five “no-neck monster” children. While sensuous Maggie “the cat” tries to work her wiles to secure a future for them, Brick spirals deeper into despair, crippled by both physical pain and emotional loss. Lurking under every practiced interaction between the Pollitts is an ulterior motive, under every smile, a challenge, and under every statement, the specter of mendacity. For the Pollitts, the truth is as hazy as the late summer sun in Mississippi, and sometimes the only way to find it is to journey through the lies. The production staged by Candlewick Players is a strong drama with mature content the characters must face as they work through the lies in their family... as a result, the play is recommended for an more mature audience.

events.description: Three generations. One stage. The hymns you grew up singing, in Winkler for one night only. BRING BACK THE HYMNS comes to the PW Enns Concert Hall on Saturday, October 17. Harvest Christian Fellowship presents a benefit concert with international violin sensation Rosemary Siemens and her family. Rosemary has performed four times at New York's Carnegie Hall and was the first violinist ever to perform in the Sistine Chapel at the Vatican since its inception in 1483. She has played in over 25 countries and 40 U.S. states, for two U.S. Presidents and Canadian Prime Ministers, and won Country Gospel Album of the Year at Canada's Gospel Music Awards. Today she leads a global movement to Bring Back the Hymns through the #1 hymn channel on YouTube, with more than 700,000 subscribers and over 200 million views in every corner of the world. This concert is that movement live and in person. Rosemary is joined by her husband, JUNO-nominated saxophonist Eli Bennett, together as the acclaimed duo SaxAndViolin, along with their young sons and Rosemary's parents. Grandparents, parents and grandchildren on one stage, playing the hymns that have been handed down through their family for generations. Expect an evening that travels from Carnegie Hall to the Vatican, from the Colosseum to the Grand Ole Opry and back home to a Manitoba church pew. Timeless hymns, inspirational classics, and the stories behind them, including how gospel music shaped Rosemary's life and continues to touch people around the world. Bring your family. Bring the people who first taught you these hymns. This is a night to sing them out loud together again. Seating is limited and this one will fill up. Get your tickets early. His options include favorite son Brick, who drinks himself into oblivion in order to bear the oppressive expectations of his determined wife, Maggie, or his less-favored son Gooper, his fertile wife Mae, and their five “no-neck monster” children. While sensuous Maggie “the cat” tries to work her wiles to secure a future for them, Brick spirals deeper into despair, crippled by both physical pain and emotional loss. Lurking under every practiced interaction between the Pollitts is an ulterior motive, under every smile, a challenge, and under every statement, the specter of mendacity. For the Pollitts, the truth is as hazy as the late summer sun in Mississippi, and sometimes the only way to find it is to journey through the lies. The production staged by Candlewick Players is a strong drama with mature content the characters must face as they work through the lies in their family... as a result, the play is recommended for an more mature audience.

events.title: If the Good Lord's Willing and the Creek Don't Rise
events.time: 7:00 PM · Manitou Opera House, 325 Main Street, Manitou, MB
events.description: This zany comedy, in the spirit of Kaufman and Hart, centers on Doc, an eccentric old man whose house caters to all sorts of characters. Now a retired judge, he spends his days “enjoying life.” When he’s not flying around the countryside in his balloon or fishing in a nearby dry riverbed, he works on his books of nonsense. This prompts his daughter, Charlotte, to decide he’s lost his marbles. So, conspiring with a sly lawyer, she plans to not only become his guardian but also sell his house and property. Throw in a psychologist on her first case, love sick teenagers, an irate school bus driver and an occasional artist or two and it’s a madhouse! Will Doc be committed or not? Of course he offers his own defense. “You ought to try tilting at a windmill every so often,” he philosophizes. “It’s great exercise and a nice breeze goes with it.” When he shows up at his sanity hearing dressed as a magician, his daughter and her lawyer think they have it all sewed up. However, Doc has a few surprise rabbits to pull out of the hat. This tour de force is appropriate for all audiences. Can Doc pull it off? As Leo says, “There is method to his madness.” And Doc shows one and all what a little nonsense can do “If the Good Lord’s Willing and the Creek Don’t Rise.” Performed by Candlewick's Manitou & Region Sr. High Drama Troupe.

events.title: Another Night of Country Music
events.time: 7:30 PM · Manitou Opera House, 325 Main Street, Manitou, MB
events.description: After packing the house with a sold-out performance in November 2025, The Sharpe Brothers Band is making a highly anticipated return to the Manitou Opera House this November - this time for two performances of Another Night of Country Music. And before anyone asks - no, they're not all brothers. The Sharpe Brothers Band features brothers Will Sharpe (vocals/guitar) and James Sharpe (vocals/bass), along with Charlie Howatt (steel guitar), Gil Dudgeon (drums), and Larry Martineau (fiddle/harmonica). A performance at the Manitou Opera House with The Sharpe Brothers Band offers a timeless country music experience reminiscent of the Grand Ole Opry, right here in southern Manitoba. Audiences can expect a show filled with traditional country music, honky-tonk favourites, outstanding musicianship, a few surprises, and the warm, intimate atmosphere that has made the historic Manitou Opera House one of southern Manitoba's premier live music venues. Their 2025 appearance at the Manitou Opera House sold out well in advance, leaving many hoping for another opportunity to experience the band live. In response to the demand, the Manitou Opera House Foundation is thrilled to welcome them back for not one, but two unforgettable showings of country music, offering audiences the opportunity to attend either - or both - shows. With last year's performance selling out, early ticket purchases are strongly encouraged. Thank you to our event sponsors: Manitou Thrift Store, Dead Horse Cider Co., and Blumstein Brewing Co. Cash bar selling beverages and snacks will be open at before the show and at intermission.
